proposed_fixes.title: Preserve external-link profile routing during web search
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: explicit browser executable/search arguments take a different profile-selection path from the registered external-URL handoff; the exact divergence is not yet demonstrated.

prerequisites: Use disposable Edge profilesAandB; makeA the default for external links andB the most recently active; retain the registered default-browser handler.
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable and current development build
steps: Open the same harmless HTTPS URL through a normal Windows external-link action and record the selected profile.
Open that URL through Run URL Handler, then run a Web Search using its explicit activation keyword.
Capture the resolved browser executable/argument pattern and compare direct search-string launch with normal URL handoff.
Repeat with Edge initially closed and already open, and regression-check a non-Edge default browser.
reproduce.expected_result: Run follows the intended registered browser/profile behavior; a divergence is assigned to the measured launch path rather than guessed profile arguments.

inferences: Launching an executable search command may enter a different Edge profile-routing path than opening an external URL. The current evidence does not establish whether the defect is in Run, registered arguments or Edge handling.
issue_context.analysis: The missing distinction is a maintainer launch-path comparison, not another generic still-happening question. Preserve user-selected browser/default-profile behavior and avoid hard-coding an Edge profile or changing every browser launch before the divergence is measured.
